articles.title: The Secret Controls GTA 6 Doesn't Tell You About — How To Flip Your Car, Flip the Bird, and Much More
articles.summary: GTA 6 has a whole bunch of secret controls that the game doesn't really tell you about. Here's how to flip your car, flip the bird, and much more.
articles.body:
There are many, many new things you can do in GTA 6 compared with the rest of the Grand Theft Auto series, and many of them have dedicated controls. One of the most obvious is the switching of sprint to L3 by default, which is explained on a menu screen before you even set foot in Leonida. Others, though, are revealed to you later in the story, or, in some cases, not outright communicated to you at all.

From how to flip your car if you end up overturning it to how you can keep the engine running outside a robbery target, here are 23 secret buttons Rockstar doesn’t tell you about in GTA 6.

1. Leaving the Car Engine Running – Want to make a quick getaway from the scene of a crime? You can leave your car’s engine purring away while you’re robbing somewhere by double-tapping the triangle/Y button on your controller when you exit the vehicle.

2. Leaving the Boat Engine Running – If you do the same thing while in a boat — double-tap the triangle/Y button — you can then freely walk around it while it continues to sail in a straight line. Use that opportunity to change into scuba gear, or shoot at nearby people if you wish.

3. Auto Drive – Want to sit back and enjoy the scenery? You can switch into cinematic camera mode and Jason or Lucia will drive to your chosen destination without you having to do a thing, much like how Red Dead Redemption 2 lets you do something similar with your horse. Hold down on the D-pad and press the options/menu button. Once in cinematic view, hold circle/B.

4. Vehicle Options – Want to manually access the options of your chosen vehicle? Open the radio menu by holding left on the D-pad, then flick the right stick to turn on your headlights, roll down the windows, or fold down the convertible roof, if your car has one. This also applies to other vehicles, such as lowering the anchor on a boat.

5. Flip Your Car – Got yourself into a little bit of bother on the tight streets of Vice City? If you happen to overturn your car completely, hit L3/LS and then hold square/X to get back onto four wheels.

6. Push Jet Ski Back Into Water – Accidentally beach your jet ski, or find one sitting on the sand that you want to get back into the ocean? Walk behind it and hold R1/RB to push it back into the water.

7. Use Your Door as a Weapon – Want to smack anyone who happens to be a little too close to your car? Tap square/X while seated inside to hit them with your door. This also works when cycling, but causes Jason or Lucia to kick out with force.

8. Get Low and Hide – Sometimes avoiding trouble is the best method, though. Avoid anyone looking for you, such as the police, by holding circle/B when sitting in the driver’s seat . Your character will then duck low to remain hidden.

9. Turn Signals – Want to fully immerse yourself when behind the wheel in GTA 6 and follow the code of the road? Tap left or right on the D-pad while driving to indicate using your turn signals.

10. Road Rage – Fancy hurling a volley of verbal abuse at a nearby driver? Yell out of the window by pressing R3/RS while driving .

11. Quick Radio Toggle – A quick double-tap of left on the D-pad when driving can swiftly switch the radio on or off if you want to make sure you hear a certain piece of dialogue, for example.

12. Hand Over the Wheel – Sometimes you just want to sit back and let your partner drive. GTA 6 lets you do this by standing near a car while playing as both Jason and Lucia together, and holding right on the D-pad and selecting cross/A .

13. Pop a Wheelie – This is one you’ve been able to do in many GTA games of the past, but it's still something that Rockstar doesn’t teach you here. Pull back on the left stick while accelerating to pop a wheelie, or push forward to perform a stoppie.

14. Car Hood Slide – There are uses for your car outside of it getting you from point A to B. It can also make you look pretty cool when on foot. Sprint and then hit cross/A when approaching a car hood to slide across it smoothly.

15. Combat Roll – If you want to go full action movie hero/heroine, then combat rolls are a necessity. Push the left stick in a direction of your choosing and hit cross/A while aiming to evade in style. Note: looks even cooler in focus mode.

16. Take a Rest – Sometimes a break from all the action is needed, though. Lean on a wall or railing by pressing R3/RS or sit on chairs or the end of a jetty by holding circle/B.

17. First-Person – Inspect Mode lets you see the world through Jason and Lucia’s eyes. While you can’t move around or drive cars from this perspective, it does let you see some of GTA 6’s details more clearly and help you find clues such as safe combinations. Hold the left trigger and then press the right stick to take a closer look.

18. Aim Down Sights – If you hit R3/RS while aiming with a gun , though, you will be able to aim down sights. This only happens if your weapon is equipped with a suitable optic, however.

19. Switch Shoulder – When aiming a weapon, you can choose which shoulder Jason or Lucia is firing from by hitting left on the D-pad .

20. Chokehold – Find yourself in a fist fight? There are plenty more ways of ending it available to you than hammering the punch button. Grapple with R2 and then hold in square/X before pressing the same button repeatedly to choke your opponent out.

21. Flip the Bird – Nothing beats the classics. Make sure you have no weapon equipped, target an NPC with the left trigger, and then hold in R1 to raise a middle finger towards them.

22. Flick the Cigarette – Another way to annoy the population of Leonida is to flick a lit cigarette into their face. Midway through smoking one, hold the left trigger and then pull the right trigger to dash the burning tobacco at them.

23.Quickly Reject Phone Calls – While it’s nowhere near as incessant as Niko’s many friends and family members ringing you in GTA 4, Jason and Lucia receive a lot of phone calls. Save yourself a few seconds and quickly reject them if you want by hitting circle/B without having to open up the phone menu. Saved you a click.

These are all of the secret buttons and prompts we’ve found so far in GTA 6, but there are likely more of them out there. Found anything we’ve missed or a particular little detail you love? Let us know in the comments.

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

articles.title: Nintendo Switch Online Just Got a Long-Awaited Update, Alongside Another GameCube Classic
articles.summary: GameCube launch title Wave Race: Blue Storm is now available via the Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack service, alongside a long-awaited new feature.
articles.body:
GameCube launch title Wave Race: Blue Storm is now available via the Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack service, alongside a long-awaited new feature.

If you're an Expansion Pack subscriber, you can now update your Nintendo Classics GameCube app to gain access to the cult classic aquatic racer — and also unlock the ability to remove the app's annoying border graphics.

The Nintendo Classic apps have a border gradient that until now you couldn't remove — and it's something that's proven a bugbear from fans who want a cleaner look. For now, only the GameCube app has the option to simply have clear black borders instead, though it seems likely the other console apps will follow. Or, maybe this is something only the technical power of Switch 2 can pull off?

"Storm warning! Prepare to ride the waves!" reads an official blurb for the game. "Take to the water in this watercraft-racing game, released for the Nintendo GameCube system in 2001. Compete in contests of speed and technique—either racing against your rivals or going up against your own records. As you race across the waves, you can see the skies changes from calm and sunny to surging storms... Weather conditions can affect visibility, water levels, and the height of the waves over the course of a race, so you'll need to be prepared for whatever comes!"

Wave Race: Blue Storm becomes the 12th GameCube title available on Switch 2 via the Expansion Pack subscription service, following the previous additions of Chibi-Robo!, F-Zero GX, Fire Emblem: Path of Radiance, Luigi's Mansion, Super Mario Strikers, Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness, SoulCalibur 2, Star Fox Adventures, Super Mario Sunshine, The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker and Wario World.

articles.title: Why is GTA 6 Getting Review Bombed?
articles.summary: Why GTA 6 user reviews are so low: Metacritic review-bombing explained.
articles.body:
GTA 6 tied with the original version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-scored game in history based on Metacritic ratings, sitting pretty at a 99 critic score. Rarely do we see something earn this kind of unanimous praise, but our reviewer Luke Reilly would agree , giving GTA 6 a coveted score of 10 on our scale and calling it “the single most impressive video game I have ever played." However, you may have heard about the wide discrepancy between the critic's metascore and the user score — as of publishing this, GTA 6 has a 5.7/10 average from well over 100,000 user reviews. Why is that?

User scores on Metacritic are under far, far (and I mean far ) less scrutiny, allowing everyone and anyone to post their own review and score regardless of how much of the game they've actually played. This isn't anything new, and it’s been around on other sites that aggregate scores from the audience (like Rotten Tomatoes or an older version of GameSpot I used to use as a kid). As a result, you're likely to see more outliers or trolling, but mostly users who shoot from the hip to let their voice be heard. That leaves things susceptible to review bombing – typically, a wave of reactionary people who have motives beyond evaluating a game for what it is.

There are reviews that appear to have legitimate concerns, mentioning that GTA 6 might not be for them or align with their tastes. Among those concerns are a slow start that emphasizes slice-of-life style activities before action starts to pick up, dissatisfaction with the interactive layers for simple tasks, the frame rate being capped at 30 fps, or a general disinterest in what it's trying to do as an open-world action game. Maybe it didn't live up to their perceived "hype" with 13 years between series entries. However, you might be wondering why GTA 6 is the latest subject of what's clearly motivated review bombing with tons of "0" scores from a reactionary crowd.

I'm not going to pretend to give credence to clearly disingenuous reviews, but if you are genuinely curious, there are a significant number of reviews that decry GTA 6 for being "too woke" and a, uh, "cuck simulator” — the most unserious people, the incel crowd coming out of the woodwork, trying to fight a weird culture war over a game they likely either did not play or have barely played. GTA has always parodied the most ridiculous parts of American culture, and GTA 6 is no exception — now the primary targets of that satire are crying about it.

I don't think I need to explain what it means to be a "cuck" or the concept of cuckoldry, but by definition, it has nothing to do with anything that happens to you or that you have to do in GTA 6. And perhaps the most telling part of it all is the complaints of "woke" (another term that has been ground to a point of no meaning, co-opted by right-wing extremists to label anything they deem politically progressive).

In large part, GTA 6 is telling a love story where two partners, the protagonists Jason and Lucia, have a believable relationship on-screen with corresponding gameplay elements in addition to their Bonnie and Clyde-esque crime sprees. Maybe you don't want to put up drywall, renovate your house, or run errands in early missions, but what you're about to read is more telling about the kind of people review-bombing the game than the content of the game itself.

Sift through the negative reviews on Metacritic and it's a trove of entries that read, "Everything that represents the woke culture don’t deserve nothing, other than zero." Or, "GTA 6 is way too woke for my taste." And other variations on one that reads, "Graphics fantastic, besides that a cuckhold [sic] game, and really woke!" One just spams the word "woke" while several are straight gibberish or admittance that they did not play the game.

One entry reads, "I already have an annoying gf in real life and you want me to deal with it in the game again???????", while another says, "No hookers, no freedom, No action, Just cuck simulator, Please woke community, leave Rockstar games alone." And (sorry) one more for the road: "The plot is boring, and the main characters are a simp and a stereotypical ‘strong woman.’ They have absolutely no charisma; the game is packed with a one-sided agenda, and the trolling of ‘libturds’ is dull and predictable."

Amid this all, Metacritic has some measures in place to moderate fake reviews — it removed user reviews that went live before the game even released . And its 36-hour rule has been in place for a while where user reviews can't go up until a day-and-a-half has passed from a game's public release. Moderators also have the ability to stamp out reviews that violate Metacritic's guidelines, but with well over 100,000 of them up now, it's a gargantuan task.

While that crowd continues to be petty, whatever dent they think they're making isn't visible, as publisher Take-Two Interactive reported $3.79 billion in revenue with approximately 32.5 million units sold by launch day. Rockstar is going to be fine. Like the game or not, outrage fatigue is settling in; this perceived culture war is as meaningless as it's ever been, and it's best to pay it no mind to save yourself from the psychic damage.

Are you playing Rockstar's blockbuster, just getting started, or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips and Chapter 2 Guide and Tips . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map .

He's usually entrusted with covering long RPGs and tech products, but he's got range when it comes to games. articles.title: GTA 6 Mandy Actor Calls Viral Fame 'Bittersweet' Because People Keep Pretending to Be Her on Social Media
articles.summary: GTA 6 actor Lexie Shoaibi has spoken out about her "bittersweet" newfound fame after her character, Mandy, went viral online.
articles.body:
GTA 6 actor Lexie Shoaibi has spoken out about her "bittersweet" newfound fame after her character, Mandy, went viral online.

Warning! Spoilers for Mandy's role in GTA 6 follow.

Lexie Shoaibi did performance capture and voice over for Mandy, a woman you meet early on in the game. Mandy asks Jason to fix a clogged sink in her house, but comes out in a tiny bikini once he’s under the sink with a wrench. It didn't take long for the internet to latch on to Mandy, with countless social media posts discussing the character.

Shoaibi appeared on a Hasan Piker stream a few days ago, chatting about GTA 6 while raising money for charity. During the stream, she spoke about the newfound fame and reaction to her character.

“I don’t know how that happened,” Shoaibi said. “People pretending to be me? It’s thrilling. Please stop, but it’s also so exciting. It’s sort of bittersweet.”

Shoaibi hinted at this issue in a seperate Instagram post in which she warned her followers about fake accounts from people trying to impersonate her on social media. Referring to one X / Twitter account that has popped up in the last week purporting to be her own, she said: "This is fake! I don’t have a Twitter! This isn’t me! Please, someone, make it go away, ew!”

Meanwhile, Shoaibi revealed she spent around 10 days on set playing Mandy, but she also did a few other NPC voices while working with Rockstar.

Warning! Specific Mandy spoilers follow.

Despite Mandy only being a minor character in Chapter 1, Rockstar’s attention to detail put a bit of a spotlight on the character. As well as her basically being nude, the garden outside Mandy’s house hides a dark secret . When Jason is fixing the sink, he finds something clogged in it. You might think it’s a chicken bone, but closer inspection shows it’s a severed human finger. Check the trunk of Mandy’s car and you can find a kill kit. Have a nosey around her back garden and you’ll find vats of acid and a freshly dug grave. The game basically hints that she’s not a harmless stalker — she’s a serial killer. No, you can’t “fix her.”

“She’s a lot of fun, so if you play the game, let me know if you find me,” Shoaibi said in another statement about her character before people made it weird. “Y’all there aren’t words!!!! Thank you so much for the love and support. This is crazy!! Ily forever!”

articles.title: Mass Effect Universe Would Have Answered Trilogy Ending Questions and Squadmate Fates, Writer Says
articles.summary: BioWare's canceled Mass Effect Universe would have addressed Mass Effect 3's controversial endings and the fates of Shepard's squadmates.
articles.body:
BioWare's canceled Mass Effect Universe would have addressed Mass Effect 3's controversial endings and the fates of Shepard's squadmates, one of the game's writers has said.

For more than a decade, Mass Effect fans have debated how BioWare could reconcile the wildly divergent endings of Mass Effect 3 — and satisfy players who insisted that their particular ending choice should be canon (I see you, Destroy fans). But according to one of the writers behind the now-canceled Mass Effect Universe, the studio had actually cracked the puzzle before EA scrapped the project and closed BioWare forever.

Speaking during a reddit fan Q&A supporting the "Save Mass Effect" fan movement, Mass Effect: Annihilation novel author Cat Valente — who spent three years on the writing team for the unfinished sequel — offered a bittersweet glimpse into how the narrative team approached the franchise's biggest lingering questions.

While strict NDAs signed with published EA continue to prevent Valente from revealing specific plot details, she emphasized that reconciling Mass Effect 3's endings was front and center for the game's writers room, and noted that the team wasn't relying on a single silver bullet to bridge the 600-year narrative gap between the original trilogy and this upcoming fifth installment.

"[We] worked specifically, and for a very long and laborious time, on handling the endings in a way that wouldn't piss everyone off, at least not piss them off completely, that wouldn't make them feel like nothing mattered, wouldn't privilege any one kind of player over another, but also allow us, somehow, to actually write a coherent story going forward, within the limits of having to do it in a playable mainstream video game and not a post-modern 3000 page novel," Valente wrote.

"Not for nothing, guys, but that's *kind of a tall f***ing order*. Part of the reason it took so long and Andromeda was in Andromeda is that figuring out an elegant solution to that problem turns out to be *really hard.* An elegant solution that we can do with current game tech, that will be approved by higher-ups, that doesn't take over the whole game and make actually telling a story impossible... it takes a long time, and it's not obvious how best to pull it off when you're the people who bear responsibility for pulling off one of, if not the, hardest nut to crack in game writing.

"And it's become really clear that it's impossible to make the gaming community completely happy with anything no matter how hard you try, especially the ME endings that were so controversial, yet people feel so strongly about their own choices. We burned out so many valuable neurons going up against that problem. I know so many people think it's easy, just make Destroy canon and move on, but consider that, for example, I feel as strongly about Synthesis as others do about Destroy. And everyone feels strongly about choices mattering. Do you really think there is a single solution that would have satisfied everyone? In a *video game*?

"But we did our best, and I think we landed in a good place," she concluded. "There wasn't one single solution, but several working together, and unfortunately I can't say any more than that."

As a hugely knowledgeable fan of the original trilogy — enough that she got the gig writing Andromeda's quarian ark prequel novel — Valente emphasized that the fates of the trilogy's loyal squadmates had also been a key consideration for the Mass Effect Universe team.

"You would have been able to know everything you wanted to know about them," she said, when asked for her own thoughts of what characters such as Garrus, Tali and Wrex did next. "I don't have headcanons about those fates, I have canon-canons. I know you'd have been able to find out about them because one of my jobs was to write all those fates and their possible variations (all then submitted to the room, workshopped with everyone, and sent to higher-ups for approval...)

"God, it was like being asked to stitch a nice border on the Shroud of Turin," she continued. "I put on my Big Writer Pants for that one and gave it every bit of talent I have, because I love those characters beyond measure, and they more than earned my best."

Of course, we know that Universe would have seen at least one fan-favorite character return: Liara, now 600 years older — around middle age for a long-lived asari. But what about others? Asked for specifics, Valente noted her NDA blocked her from confirming specific names, but that there had been widespread discussion of bringing back every character possible.

"I think the best way to answer your question is to say that any character who physically *could* survive, we considered allowing to survive into the new game and made decisions on them," Valente teased. "We thought about all the things you'd have wanted us to think about, and I hope you do believe that, because it's the truth. Everyone in that room loved those characters, or loved to hate them, as much as any fan. We took each and every one of them and their fates very seriously."

So, who could have survived? Alongside the asari, the krogan are another long-lived Mass Effect species — and some fans believe we already got a glimpse at an older Grunt in the krogan civil war artwork released by BioWare a couple of years ago. Could Wrex also still be around? While he'd be ancient, it would not be impossible. Synthetic characters like EDI could certainly be around (and even if you'd picked Destroy, could surely have been rebooted eventually from a backup).

And then there are the characters and plotlines from Andromeda — a game that's nowhere near as beloved as the original Mass Effect trilogy, but whose storyline was still expected to factor into Universe in some way. Indeed, Valente revealed, Andromeda fans would have finally gained the answer to some of the spinoffs lingering questions (which were originally set to be answered in long-scrapped Andromeda sequels). For example, fans would have finally learned the identity of The Benefactor, who funded the Milky Way galaxy's push to Andromeda for unclear reasons.

"There is an answer, and it was fucking rad," Valente said. "As the author of an Andromeda tie-in, I and one of the other writers [...] worked closely on closing out Andromeda mysteries and bringing it together with the rest of the story. We know who [The Benefactor] was. At least the six of us in the writers' room know, plus anyone who approved our narratives or saw our work in-progress. I wish I could tell you, sorry."

11 Mass Effect Characters and Moments the TV Show Needs to Be a Hit

Finally, and least surprisingly, Valente confirmed that Universe would have featured new aliens alongside the returning characters/races from the four games so far. (Would the bird-like raloi finally have appeared on-screen? We will now never know.)

"I don't think there's a problem with saying of course there were going to be new aliens?" Valente concluded. "We all pitched new species and some were accepted and moved along to art etc and some weren't. Same with the squad. All of us pitched squad members and our directors chose between the pitches. I can't give you any more than that."

While EA has officially canceled Mass Effect Universe and BioWare's offices have now closed their doors, fans are trying their best to show there's still huge interest in the franchise — even if any sort of U-turn on EA's decision currently seems unlikely. Some fans have suggested EA could alternatively be convinced to sell the Mass Effect IP to another publisher who would do something with it, but again this seems a remote possibility. EA can simply hold onto the franchise rights to leverage it in other games (N7 skins in Battlefield, anyone?) and continue profiting from ongoing merchandise and licensing revenue.

It remains a heartbreaking end for Mass Effect, though there is of course one glimmer of hope remaining: the not-yet-canceled Mass Effect TV series that remains in development for Prime Video. Should this ever escape development hell and make it to release and be a success and convince EA it should give Mass Effect another go... well, maybe we'd find out what Grunt was doing 600 years later after all.

articles.title: GTA 6 - PlayStation 5 Pro Vs Base PlayStation 5 | Graphics Comparison - IGN
articles.summary: After three playstation generations of waiting, Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here.  And while it’s advertised that it plays best on PlayStation, is that actually the case? In this video we’re going to look at the graphical differences between the game running on a base PlayStation 5 vs a PlayStation 5 pro. On the base Playstation 5 you’re going to get the game outputting at an upscaled 4K resolution from an internal 1440p that runs at a solid 30 fps. The upscaling is a bit softer on the base PS5 due to it not using PSSR like the PS5 Pro, but that’s not to say the game is blurry or anything. There are also some instances where the frame rate can drop to a sub-20fps, but that’s few and far in-between.  The base PS5 does feature Ray Tracing, but it’s not as robust as the more expensive Pro will get you. Speaking of the PS5 Pro. If you’re using Sonys flagship box you will also get an upscaled 4K resolution that is a little sharper thanks to PSSR, but it’s still pulling from an internal 1440p resolution. Ray Tracing is more robust on the Pro and that 30fps stays more consistent thanks to the additional horsepower under the PS5 Pro’s hood. Regardless of how you play GTA 6, you’re definitely in for a game that plays as good as it looks.

Regardless of how you play GTA 6, you’re definitely in for a game that plays as good as it looks.

articles.title: Disney+ and Hulu Bundle Drops to $4.99/Month for Black Friday 2026
articles.body:
Disney+ has officially revealed its Black Friday deal for 2026 , and of course the streaming service is bringing Hulu along for the ride.

From now until November 30, both new and eligible returning subscribers can get the Disney+ and Hulu bundle (with ads) for $4.99/month . The deal applies to a full 12-month period, covering you until the next round of Black Friday discounts.

We’ve been seeing fewer and fewer streaming deals over the past year, so this is 100% your best chance to save on either service until 2027. The discount matches the Disney+ and Hulu deal from 2025 , though after another round of price hikes (which are pretty much annual now), it technically nets you even better savings this time around.

Disney+ and Hulu Black Friday Deal Now Live

The streaming deal knocks $8 off the monthly cost of the Disney+ and Hulu bundle, which otherwise costs $12.99/month. The discount runs for a full year, offering $96 in savings over the course of 12 months.

The plan will renew at the “then-current monthly retail price” after the deal period ends. The bundle is currently priced at $14.99/month, but that language leaves room for another price hike before Black Friday 2027. Disney+ has raised prices the past four years in a row, so getting the Black Friday deal is definitely the best way to play a little price hike defense.

The Disney+ and Hulu bundle discount is the only discount being offered by either service. Unfortunately, you won’t find any savings on the ad-free bundle, annual plan, or standalone Disney+ and Hulu accounts. We’re also not seeing deals on any Disney+ bundle with other services, though HBO Max has its own standalone offer .

As for what the bundle will get you, the short answer is a lot. Unlike services like Peacock , any Disney+ and Hulu subscription gets you access to both services’ full libraries.

For Disney+, that includes all of the animated Disney and Pixar classics in addition to its ongoing slate of new releases , like Percy Jackson and the Olympians. Disney is also home to all things Star Wars and, if you're still doing homework for Avengers: Doomsday , where you'll find all of the MCU.

The Hulu side is a bit more chaotic, but that can be a serious benefit when for finding hidden gems. While it hosts its fair share of movies, Hulu is a real hub for TV, featuring original programs like Only Murders in the Building as well as licensed series like Abbott Elementary, Always Sunny in Philadelphia, and Grey’s Anatomy.

The Full Slate of Black Friday Streaming Deals

If you’re looking specifically for an ad-free streaming deal, your best bet is Apple TV , Paramount+ , or, if you’re into the anime scene, Crunchyroll .

The rest of the major Black Friday streaming slate — including Peacock and HBO Max — have limited their discounts to ad-supported plans. Still, these deals are the best way to save on any streaming library for at least the next couple of months.

articles.title: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 Teaser Pretty Much Confirms Fifth Playable Faction — and the Appearance of a Would-Be Chaos God
articles.summary: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 is almost upon us, and publisher Plaion has released a new trailer that teases the appearance of a fan-favorite character from the tabletop game — and even the fifth playable faction.
articles.body:
Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 is almost upon us, and publisher Plaion has released a new trailer that teases the appearance of a fan-favorite character from the tabletop game — and even the fifth playable faction.

Dawn of War 4, developed by King Art Games, launches with four playable races: the Space Marines; Orks, Necrons, and the Adeptus Mechanicus. We knew that the developer had plans to release more factions over time, as has been the case with previous entries in the real-time strategy series. But we didn’t know which would come first… until now.

Warning! Potential spoilers for Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 follow.

The teaser ends with a tease for Dawn of War 4’s first DLC faction. We see the unmistakable eyes of Vashtorr the Arkifane, alongside the narration: “And what began on Aurelia is coming to Kronus.”

That’s a clear reference to Chaos as the new faction, given Aurelia, the former homeworld and capital of the Blood Ravens Space Marine Chapter, was gobbled up by the Warp (Warhammer 40,000’s version of a hell dimension full of demons), before it was spat out and besieged by Black Legion Chaos Space Marines. So, it would make sense that Chaos Space Marines are the new faction. Will we see further corruption of the Blood Ravens play out?

But what about Vashtorr the Arkifane? Vashtorr is a sort of in-between, Chaos Undivided being who appears to have designs on becoming the fifth Chaos god. According to the lore, Vashtorr came into existence within the Warp due to our obsessive pursuit of tech innovation (feels pretty relatable right now, doesn’t it?). As such, Vashtorr acts as a sort of arms dealer to the existing Chaos factions, creating powerful daemon weapons and engines for use in war.

Ever since Vashtorr’s dramatic introduction into the Warhammer 40,000 universe with the Arks of Omen storyline a few years ago, and his uneasy alliance with Horus’ successor, Abaddon the Despoiler, fans have wondered about his masterplan. As is Games Workshop’s want, the overarching Warhammer 40,000 storyline moves slowly, so we don’t really have much to go on beyond he’s big, he’s mean, and he wants it all. Perhaps Dawn of War 4 will shed more light on his motivations?

Either way, it would be really cool if we got to actually command Vashtorr on the battlefield, although you’d expect him to be incredibly overpowered, given what we know of his power set from the lore. Dawn of War 4 is the first Warhammer 40,000 video game to feature a playable Primarch (one of the Emperor’s ultra powerful sons). Could we see Lion El'Jonson go up against Vashtorr in the DLC? That would be quite something.

It’s not long before we find out. Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 launches on PC on December 3, 2026.

articles.title: I Watched GTA 6's In-Game TV Shows For Hours, They're Absolutely Wild
articles.summary: Rockstar's satire has reached new levels with in-game cartoons like Barnyard Blue and the dark comedy The Tyrone Show.
articles.body:
Of all the things I expected of Grand Theft Auto 6, sitting there watching in-game TV for like…two hours was not on my list. Freshly pre-loaded and ready to go on my Xbox Series X right at 3am on the west coast, claiming to be in New Zealand, booting it up for the first time had me rubbing my hands like Birdman – I was ready to get in the thick of it in GTA 6. What could this new Vice City's criminal underworld make me do? Not much. Will I have to survive shootouts early on, and will I need to contend with the new wanted system in a car chase? Not really. Mostly because as soon as I got to Jason's home in the opening hour, I sat my ass down on his living room couch, flipped on Weazel News and couldn't believe what I was seeing.

In GTA 6, you can sit on the couch and flip through three TV channels of original in-universe programming – full on TV shows made for the game, existing within the fiction of its world. You have Weazel News, the nutty right-wing parody that broadcasts news segments and TV series with the production value of something we'd see in our real world. Then there's the Telemundo spoof called Megamundo that shows Spanish-language soap operas / telenovelas, but with the absurdity cranked up several notches. Lastly, there's the Visit Leonida channel that's dedicated to advertising tourist attractions and businesses across this fictional rendition of Florida, satirizing modern economics and business.

And no, these are not channels with maybe a couple minutes' worth of gags to see once and move on from – these act as legit television programming, shows with multiple episodes that go on for six to eight minutes each. Why would I flip through my free Roku channels or be hit with choice paralysis on my own TV's built-in streaming apps when GTA 6 could rapid fire some of the wildest shit the series has done with shows you'd never see on real TV?

I'd get a kick out of Alan Wake 2's Koskela Brothers commercials or Max Payne's Adventures of Captain Baseball Bat Boy episodes, which aligned with Remedy's style and universe. But it's kind of astonishing that GTA 6's level of production value for in-game entertainment would rival or exceed cable TV – if someone was going to do it, though, it'd be Rockstar.

Weazel is by far the most intricate channel, weaving in anchored news segments and on-the-ground reporting that take ridiculous right-wing talking points and conspiracy theories to seed its own brand of misinformation across Leonida. In between these reports are legitimately produced TV shows to further clown on this type of extremist politics through shock humor.

Barnyard Blue is straight-up cop propaganda masked as a children's cartoon with an aggressive blonde child partnering with anthropomorphic animals "solving" crimes on a farm, clearly satirizing police brutality and abuse of power by law enforcement you see in the real world. One episode ends with the child monologuing the lesson, "Don't question authority silly! Respect the chain of command like your life depends on it, and one day, you'll be the law and can do, well, pretty much anything you like!"

Right Wing is an Adult Swim-style animated superhero series where the titular eagle-themed "hero" tries "saving America" from its "societal ills" – it highlights the projection and hypocrisy of modern conservative politics with regard to LGBTQ+, but done in such an over-the-top and comedic fashion that either has me cringing or cracking up. In one episode, a villain called "The Flamer" captures the President and has him tied up and in a ball gag. Right Wing gets word about the situation from inside a gay club and exclaims, "Repression builds character, dammit! Not on my watch!" He then busts into the Oval Office, confronting The Flamer with, "Get your beautifully manicured hands off the President!" In an attempt to save the President from being kissed by The Flamer, he dives in and ends up kissing The Flamer.

The Johnsons is another animated series made in the vein of Family Guy that centers around a family of…anthropomorphic (?)...penises…who try adjusting to a new community full of free-spirited neighbors, and highlights the absurdity of social conservatism. You'll see husband and wife Hugh and Wanda meet their new neighbors who are a couple they mistakenly think are inviting them to a sex party and end up at a very normal get-together in BDSM gear. "She shows me she loves me by stuffing my nuts into a little bird cage, but that's us. The important thing is remembering why you fell in love in the first place," the neighbors conclude. To which Hugh tells Wanda, "Oh honey, you know I'd let you rearrange my balls like origami anytime."

Then there's The Tyrone Show which is a mockumentary-style sitcom about Tyrone and his increasingly ridiculous, unhinged dating life in Vice City – it's meant to mock the modern dating scene in cities like Miami and takes cues from The Vince Staples show. With the slapstick, hostile nature, I'm still trying to work out whether its satire is problematic, hilarious, or mean-spirited, or all of those things in combination, and maybe that's the point? All I know is the acting performances are incredible and I can't look away, and maybe that's also the point.

Trying to gauge Rockstar-style satire and whether or not its commentary is poignant, that's something we'll probably be stewing on for a good long while. Regardless, there's no denying that this is the studio's biggest effort building out an in-world fiction. The Megamundo telenovelas got crazy twists that put those reruns of Cuna de Lobos in the background of my grandma's house to shame.

The Visit Leonida channel features PSAs from the state government to warn them about wildlife outbreaks and the governor's pretty fucked-up crusade against furries. Those are interstitials between hysterical ad spots for the likes of car detailing shops, restaurants, and lawyers that spoof on American commercials for genuine laugh-out-loud moments. Tourism stingers poke at glorifying gentrification, overindulgence, and ads that play on selling working-class people on faux lavish lifestyles. Of course, GTA's advantage is not having to abide by FCC regulations, and that it's a video game after all – you can mock your audience all you want.

Vice City being based on Miami, GTA 6 is sprinkled with Cuban culture and brushes right up on the line of stereotypes. One commercial rapidly fires off all the services immigrants may need – "Need a notarized affidavit for your cousin's immigration papers? Boom. And we got pin pan puns, too! (Aye coño!) A new ID and a set of 26-inch rims? Hit up 'I Know A Guy'" If you're from this part of the world, these jokes do play into something very familiar to us (and referencing a pin pan pun tells me someone Cuban definitely wrote this commercial).

As our GTA 6 reviewer Luke Reilly said , there are many, many distractions, most of which are great. In my early hours in Leonida, watching TV has been the greatest one yet, and it's going to be tough to top. So, if you have some downtime between missions, housework, errands, or heists, check out GTA 6's TV shows for the dark realization of how our world is a real messed-up place, but one where you may as well get some laughs out of it along the way.

articles.title: GTA 6 Players Are Optimizing the Money Glitch to Within an Inch of Its Life to Make $100,000 in Just 10 Minutes
articles.summary: We’ve already covered players using infinite money glitches to get rich quickly in GTA 6, but people are taking it to the next level. New money-making optimization strategies are seeing players become millionaires in a couple of hours, while still in the early game.
articles.body:
We’ve already covered players using infinite money glitches to get rich quickly in GTA 6 , but people are taking it to the next level. New money-making optimization strategies are seeing players become millionaires in a couple of hours, while still in the early game.

Instead of playing the game as intended and robbing stores, banks, and gang hideouts, some GTA 6 players are repeating the same actions over and over to generate money fast.

The new method sees players using vans and character swaps at a location in a town called Hamlet. In Hamlet, there’s an industrial area with a big warehouse outside of town, with a teddy bear van parked outside.

There are drugs inside the van outside as well as inside the warehouse itself. To do the glitch, you need to register two vans, turn up to the location, and have your partner call in a different personal vehicle while the player calls in one of the personal vans and takes the loot.

Stow the loot in the back of your personal vehicle, then drive the teddy van parked outside into the warehouse, parking it inside, on the right of the door, at which point tell your partner to wait in the car. The player then gets out and drives the teddy bear van parked inside (both of these vans are empty of loot at this point) and park this opposite the other van, so both vans have their back doors facing the shutter entrance.

Next, switch to your partner and exit the first teddy van before heading outside, where you switch back. Then ask your partner to drive the personal van loaded with all the loot. Using the partner menu, ask your partner to fence the loot, and watch them drive off to do so.

Once your partner has driven off, use the Scooter Bros app to call in the second personal van. After backing the van up to the warehouse, switch to the partner fencing the loot, before immediately switching back. This respawns both teddy bear vans and the loot inside, but it also keeps the two you moved earlier where you parked them inside and fills them with loot, essentially doubling the take.

According to one GTA 6 player who posted about this new method on Reddit , the technique earns you between $88,000-$100,000 in under 10 minutes.

Some of the replies to the Reddit post asked the OP when their in-game bank account limit will be raised, suggesting they’re still relatively early in the game. Later on, more lucrative robbery opportunities open up for players anyway, and you can pull off $100k jobs with way less hassle than this, and while having some actual fun whilst you’re at it.

The question is whether Rockstar patches early days money glitches like these out of GTA 6. GTA 6's first post-launch patch failed to take action, but I imagine it won't be long before Rockstar does something about this.

articles.title: Scott Pilgrim and Ramona Flowers Join Fortnite This Week
articles.summary: Scott Pilgrim takes on the world of Fortnite later this week, with the battle royale's next crossover. Check out this first look.
articles.body:
Scott Pilgrim takes on the world of Fortnite later this week, with the battle royale's next crossover.

Character skins for Scott Pilgrim and Ramona Flowers will become available via the Shop for an as-yet undisclosed amount of V-Bucks. To be clear, these are the graphic novel versions of the characters — so no Michael Cera in Fortnite, yet.

Epic Games announced the collaboration today via a teaser trailer showing off both character skins in action (Ramona has multiple hair style options, I can see), riffing on the story's plot of Scott defeating a league of evil ex-partners.

They’re not playing games anymore! Scott Pilgrim and Ramona Flowers are coming to Fortnite this week. — Fortnite (@Fortnite) November 24, 2026

They’re not playing games anymore! Scott Pilgrim and Ramona Flowers are coming to Fortnite this week.

Other Fortnite shenanigans we've learned of today: a Puss in Boots collaboration is next on the docket (and yes, Puss will be a pet-like Sidekick) before the current mini-season is done. Speaking of which, Fortnite's big year-end live event is currently slated for December 5, which is also when the game will hold its next Community Day.

Hop into Fortnite then for a smattering of free cosmetics, watch on Twitch for a free golden Jonesy skin, and if you've picked up at least 800 V-Bucks at some point this season you'll get the long-teased pirate Hope skin. Exactly what's set to happen during the event remains to be seen, but the stage is set for Fortnite's uber big bad Geno to finally get his come-uppance (again), while the mysterious Captain X will reveal his true identity after recently crashing a real-life awards show. Here's hoping it's not Mr. Beast.

How's Fortnite doing right now? The launch of GTA 6 has naturally had some impact on its daily active player count, though Alinea Analytics noted the battle royale had recovered well following Rockstar's big launch last week. The same cannot be said for Call of Duty , with active HQ users down 40% since GTA 6's launch. It seems fair to suggest that COD's audience is more aligned with GTA's, but Fortnite has also reaped the rewards of its current mini-season allowing players to win a fortnight of free access to the game's Shop — something many players have been grinding for, despite low odds .

What's next for Fortnite? While Epic Games boss Tim Sweeney spends his time on X / Twitter discussing AI and various other subjects, his team will launch the game's Chapter 8 incarnation following that December 8 in-game event. As of yet, nothing major has leaked for what's in store.
